name: Pirate
summary: Pirates and buccaneers are lawless seafaring plunderers operating across the Great Sea and coastal waters of Azeroth. Preying on Alliance, Horde, and neutral merchant vessels alike, they band together under loose flags to seize wealth, capture cargo, and control coastal coves. Their violent presence drives constant naval skirmishes from the waters of Kalimdor to the shores of the Eastern Kingdoms.

sections.title: Lords of the High Seas
sections.body: Pirates—often called buccaneers, corsairs, or freebooters—are maritime raiders of nearly every race who make their living seizing ships and raiding coastal settlements. Their operations stretch far beyond simple robbery; crews regularly engage in smuggling, kidnappings, and mercenary contracts for whoever has coin. With the chaos left behind by the Third War and the collapse of northern kingdoms, naval enforcement has fractured, giving pirate factions the freedom to carve out fortified footholds on neglected islands and coastal coves.

sections.title: A Ruthless Life
sections.body: Despite common tales painting pirate life as one of romantic adventure, life aboard a buccaneer vessel is brutal and short. Crews endure squalid, rat-infested holds, harsh discipline, and the ever-present threat of scurvy, fought off only with supplies of limes. Betrayal is an everyday hazard, and captains maintain their command solely through strength and fear of punishment, which ranges from immediate execution to being marooned or fed to sharks. When battles end, buccaneers celebrate with roaring bouts of dice, song, and heavy rum.

sections.title: Factions and Havens
sections.body: While independent crews roam every sea lane, major organizations wield enough ships to contest sovereign navies. The Southsea Freebooters harass shipping throughout the waters surrounding Kalimdor, while the notorious Bloodsail Buccaneers menace the southern seas and wage open war against the Steamwheedle Cartel in Booty Bay.

faq.q: What is the difference between a pirate, buccaneer, and freebooter?
faq.answer: The titles are largely used interchangeably along the sea lanes of Azeroth. While some groups prefer particular banners—such as the Southsea Freebooters or the Bloodsail Buccaneers—they all engage in maritime raiding, robbery, smuggling, and coastal plundering.

faq.q: Where are the main pirate bases located?
faq.answer: Pirate crews congregate in lawless anchorages and hidden harbors across the world. Major havens include Plunder Isle and coastal camps scattered throughout the shores of Tanaris, the Barrens, and Stranglethorn Vale.

Most pirate crews are indiscriminate predators. They hunt merchant vessels, civilian transports, and military supply craft belonging to the Alliance, the Horde, and the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel alike. Any ship laden with gold, timber, or trade goods is a potential target.

faq.q: How do pirate crews recruit new members?
faq.answer: Pirates expand their numbers by hiring desperate cutthroats and mercenaries in port towns, but they also rely heavily on press-ganging. Captured sailors and travelers are frequently given the choice between swearing fealty to the crew or being cast into the sea.

faq.q: How does Kul Tiras deal with pirates?
faq.answer: Kul Tiran law treats piracy as one of the most vile offenses a sailor can commit. Those captured by Kul Tiran patrols face immediate death by public execution, though rare crews have managed to secure royal pardons by undertaking perilous, high-stakes tasks for the admiralty.

Yes. While human crews are common, buccaneer crews accept anyone willing to raid and follow orders. Crews include orcs, goblins, trolls, dwarves, and even tauren who were recruited or impressed into service along the coasts of Kalimdor.

angles.text: The cutthroat tactics, blinding powder, and swift blade work of pirate crews closely mirror the practical, lethal fighting styles favored by roguish mercenaries.
Alliance transport lines between Stormwind, Ironforge, and Theramore are under constant threat from buccaneers who prowl coastal trade routes.
The Southsea Freebooters maintain aggressive encampments along the coast of Durotar and the Barrens, raiding Horde caravans and landing parties.
Though plains dwellers by tradition, some tauren traveling Kalimdor's shores have ended up aboard pirate vessels, either impressed into crews or seeking fortune.
